identity: Copperline is an old believable fictional hosting provider and community archive with accumulated human history. It is a recurring modern evidence surface, not a thin address-recovery prologue or obvious ARG portal.

c01_ladder_boundary.exact_earned_belief: mkept was a real person who deliberately preserved a damaged server
c01_ladder_boundary.ancient_truth_boundary: Users discuss servers, files, footage, builds, disappearances, anomalies, and one another. Ancient truth reaches Copperline only through recovered artifacts and modern interpretation.

information_architecture.content: mundane server listings, status history, mirrors, categories, dead projects, and ordinary neighboring listings
profiles, signatures, avatars, joins, last activity, edits, reactions, public history, and privacy-respecting gaps
tickets, staff replies, escalations, maintenance notices, outage incidents, attachment custody, and bureaucratic closure states
posts, comment threads, quoted replies, guides, arguments, moderation artifacts, removed posts, cached excerpts, and archival gaps
changelogs, build notes, filenames, checksums, mirrors, broken embeds, cached or dead attachments, and version relationships
later annotations, unlocks, recovered mirrors, and changed availability that preserve immutable prior versions and catch-up readback

content_density_standard.direct_clue_definition: An entry whose primary authored job is to supply an immediately actionable investigation fact, key, answer component, or provenance link.
content_density_standard.texture_definition: An entry whose primary job is ordinary hosting/community life, relationship, humor, work, disagreement, frustration, care, or historical context, whether or not it later gains meaning.
content_density_standard.planning_ratio: Across each substantial cold-readable archive slice, direct clues should ordinarily be no more than one part for at least three parts texture; mixed or later-recontextualized entries require human classification.
content_density_standard.anti_padding_rule: The ratio is a credibility alarm, not a prose quota. Do not fabricate filler, repeat voices, or lower writing quality to satisfy a count.
content_density_standard.human_gate: A cold reader should encounter convincing unrelated life before recognizing the archive as evidence, and should not assume every username, error, or broken link is a puzzle.

procedural but human; uneven judgment, edits, warnings, conflict fatigue, and context loss

time_layers.function: credible hosting and community life before the central anomaly dominates attention
C01 support tickets, listings, mirrors, and mkept activity earn the exact onboarding belief
build excitement, footage debate, technical anomalies, interpersonal strain, disappearances, and abandoned plans accumulate without early spoilers
removed material, abandoned accounts, failed embeds, mirrors, moderation actions, and conflicting memories show human and technical breakage
players revisit history, observe newly meaningful chronology and provenance, and trigger honest append-only reactions or availability changes
new Minecraft, NPC, footage, or document evidence changes the reading of preserved posts while the old bytes/history remain inspectable

natural_clue_locations: account behavior, edits, last activity, and moderation history
removed material with honest archival gaps
usernames and filenames only when fictionally grounded
questions people avoid, misunderstand, or fail to answer
historical posts reinterpreted after later evidence
human_texture_examples_non_exhaustive: concern for someone who stopped posting
arguments about whether a recording was staged
apologies and repaired or unrepaired relationships
evidence of the prior company fracturing
disagreement_rule: Posts and tickets may disagree because of memory, embarrassment, bureaucracy, incomplete information, loyalty, conflict, or self-protection. Users are people, not cryptic puzzle dispensers.
callback_opportunities_non_exhaustive: an old support phrase becomes important only after a Minecraft system message repeats it
a quoted reply preserves text removed from the original post
a footage filename makes an old changelog edit or mirror sequence newly relevant
an NPC memory changes which participant a vague pronoun or apology referred to
a later document version explains why two staff replies used identical language
an ordinary build screenshot contains a detail that matters only after the Hold is understood
a user's silence, edit pattern, or abandoned draft becomes emotional evidence rather than an answer token
